title: Low-touch leasepool failsafe for cross-region KV & stream backends
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a low-coordination connection leasing pool (leasepool) and proportional degrade strategy that provides predictable SLO behavior for Redis/KV, Kafka, and primary DBs across multi-region traffic. The goal is a light-touch mechanism that throttles connections per-tenant/route, gives deterministic soft-failover behavior during downstream saturation, and enables fast recovery with minimal global coordination.
background: We've observed cascading failures when regional KV/Kafka stalls cause connection queues to grow and then exhaust global connection budgets. Current connpool strategies either centrally coordinate (high complexity) or simply close connections (high customer impact). This ticket experiments with 'leases' issued locally that grant short-lived connection budgets, plus a proportional degrade model that steps through graceful fallback modes (local cache, degraded responses, read-only, enqueue-only) before hard failures.
implementation_plan: 1) Implement local lease allocator in connpool: each node maintains a small local budget and periodically refreshes a lease token bucket from a regional allocator. 2) Add per-tenant priority lanes (system, gold, standard, best-effort) enforced by lease weight. 3) Implement degrade handlers: prefix-KV skip, read-only flag for DB calls, kafka-enqueue-backpressure with local spill-to-disk, and a cached-response path for common embeddings. 4) Circuit-breaker integration: leases count toward circuit budgets; repeated failures reduce lease size with exponential backoff. 5) Expose metrics and feature flags: lease_size, lease_refresh_rate, per-lane_admit_rate. 6) Integration tests and chaos scenarios (region partition, slow redis, kafka broker OOM).
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end tests demonstrating sustained 99th-percentile tail under simulated KV latency increase by 10x for 5 minutes.
- Per-tenant SLOs maintained for P99 latency of critical routes or gracefully fall through to documented degrade modes.
- Automated canary demonstrating no increased error budget for 'gold' tenants during test.
- Documentation (playbook + runbook) added to Confluence with exact rollback steps.
- Performance: lease bookkeeping adds <1% CPU overhead at p95 query rates.
- Meaningful dashboards: per-tenant admission, lease refill failures, degrade mode activations.
metrics:
- Admission rate by lane (per-second)
- Lease refill success ratio
- Per-tenant P50/P95/P99 latency on KV/DB/Kafka paths
- Fraction of requests served from degraded path
- Recovery time (time from downstream recovery to full admission)
- Error budget burn rate during experiments
rollout_plan:
Phase 1: feature-flag off in staging, run chaos experiments and performance benchmarks.
Phase 2: gated canary (5% production traffic) targeting non-critical tenants for 48 hours; monitor metrics and runbooks.
Phase 3: expand to 25% with more tenants and another 48-hour soak.
Phase 4: global rollout with per-region thresholds, enable automatic scaleback rules.
Rollback: flip feature flag off and revert lease config; have scripts to drain local lease queues and re-open original connpool.
risks:
- Incorrect lease sizing could starve high-priority tenants or cause oscillation.
- Lease refresh coordinator could become a scaling hotspot if implemented naively.
- Spill-to-disk for Kafka enqueue may introduce disk pressure and complicate recovery.
- Interaction with existing autoscalers: transient drop in admitted traffic could confuse horizontal scaling heuristics.
- Risk of silent data loss if degraded write modes aren't correctly bounded and reconciled.
mitigations:
- Start with conservative default lease sizes and expose runtime flags.
- Implement coordinator as a best-effort leaky token refiller with exponential backoff and local jitter.
- Enforce strict caps and TTLs on spill-to-disk queues; implement reconciliation job.
- Coordinate with infra autoscaling team to add lease-admission signals as a stable metric.
- Add end-to-end invariants and periodic reconciliation checks for write-degrade modes.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for lease allocation, refill, and backoff.
- Integration test harness that injects latency/failures into Redis, Kafka, and primary DB.
- Chaos experiments: region partition, disk saturation, broker restarts.
- Load test with tenant mix to validate weighted admission and priority lanes.
- UAT: invite two internal product teams to validate behavior on simulated failure windows.
observability_and_alerting:
- New dashboards: lease_health (per-region), per-tenant_admission, degrade_mode_activations.
- Alerts: lease_refill_fail_rate > 5% for 5m, degrade_mode_activation_rate spike, recovery_time > target.
- Runbook: step-by-step restore including commands to drain leases, escalate to runway team, and trigger fallback proxies.
- Track postmortem links for all chaos runs.
notes: Related RFC in Google Doc: 'Leasepool for low-coordination connection budgets' (link in Confluence). Expect follow-up tickets for on-disk spill reconciliation and tenant billing adjustments. Include SRE review before Phase 2. Include SDK changes for routing hints.
